picks.why: Family winery in the town of Goumenissa, in its present form since 1978 by one account, with a family history of wine said to go back more than a century; its Goumenissa is the appellation's blend of Xinomavro and Negoska.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the house bottles a Goumenissa and a single vineyard Goumenissa, both stocked by Greek merchants, the single vineyard wine given as seven parts Xinomavro to three of Negoska in a London magazine's tasting. The author confirms which label is the one to know (the plain Goumenissa stands unless the single vineyard wine proves the one a guest meets), the founding (1978 for the present winery comes from one merchant and the earlier family date is unconfirmed: leave founded empty unless two agree) and whether the two grapes are fermented together, which the lane's why said the law asks and this run could not confirm. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Organic family estate at Filyria in the Goumenissa zone that works the appellation's blend and its grapes one by one; its Goumenissa is Xinomavro with about three parts in ten of Negoska.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the Goumenissa carries the PDO and is stocked under this name in Greece and Britain as seven parts Xinomavro to three of Negoska, and the vineyards at Filyria are farmed organically by a Greek Master of Wine's account. The author confirms the certification and its year, the founding (1994 in one glossary, perhaps the planting and not the winery: leave founded empty unless two agree) and the label's spelling (Chatzivaritis on export labels, Chatzivariti and Hatzivaryti at Greek merchants). The varietal Negoska, the Xinomavro bottled alone and the Roditis go in others, none of them the appellation's wine. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Goumenissa family estate in its third generation, growing vines since 1924 by one account and farmed organically with little done in the cellar; its Goumenissa, first made in 1997 and released after long ageing, is the one met on natural wine lists abroad.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the Goumenissa carries the PDO (a natural wine fair's sheet for the 2009 and a second account), so the pick stands; the house's old vine Xinomavro has no Negoska and cannot carry it, and goes in others with the young vine red. The author confirms 1924 from two sources or leaves founded empty, the first vintage of 1997, the organic certification (1998 in one account) and the blend, given as equal parts in some vintages and seven to three in another: teach it without a fixed share. The lane's wild yeast, little sulphur and no filtration were not confirmed here. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: An older Goumenissa winery at the foot of Mount Paiko, taken over in 2018 by the founders of Ktima Biblia Chora and renamed; its Goumenissa is the classic blend of about four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the estate is at Dyo Potamia by the northern winemakers' association's own page, its Goumenissa is stocked in Greece, Britain and Norway as four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska, and two accounts tell of the takeover, one of them giving 2018. The author confirms the year from a second source, the founding of the winery before it under its founder's own name, and the label's spelling (Titos abroad, Titou in Greek). The varietal Negoska goes in others. Name no living person of either house.

picks.why: The Naoussa house's own winery at Goumenissa, at work since 1984 and for many years the only one in the district, with an organic estate vineyard at Filyria planted in 1991; its Goumenissa is a large house's wine of the appellation, made in the zone.
picks.note: Pick in doubt, for the merge agent to rule. Boutari is already Naoussa's pick in plan.json, and that pick's note sends its Goumenissa to others under the rule of one flagship a producer. The winery is entered here under its own name because the appellation has five bottlers this run could confirm and this is the fifth: the house's own page heads it Winery of Goumenissa, Domaine Filyria, and Wines of Greece lists it apart from the Naoussa cellar. If the rule holds, drop this pick and the group stands at four, since no sixth house could be confirmed. If the pick stays, amend the Naoussa note, and the author confirms from the house which wine is the one to know and carries the PDO (the Goumenissa, or the estate wine Filyria, spelt Filiria in some sources), the dates of 1984 and 1991 from a second source, and that the winery is at work and bottling under this name. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Name no living member of the family.
